title: File
body:
[[Bash file]]
[[Directory]]

---

Named storage that outlives the program. Two senses in this course:

**Files you work in.** Source (`.cpp`), headers (`.h`), and the executable `g++` produces.
Organised into [[Directory|directories]] and reached from the [[Shell]]. See
[[Interface Module]] for why a class ends up split across two of them.

**Files the program reads and writes.** `#include <fstream>`:

```c++
ifstream in("data.txt");
if (!in) { cerr << "cannot open"; return 1; }

int x;
while (in >> x)      // stops at end of file, same as the eof [[Sentinel]] pattern
	cout << x << endl;
in.close();
```

`ifstream` reads, `ofstream` writes, and once open they behave like `cin` and `cout`. Always
check that the open succeeded; reading from a stream that failed to open gives garbage, which
is the [[Runtime Errors|runtime error]] version of forgetting. `in.eof()` is the file case of
[[Sentinel]]-controlled repetition.

What a file actually is (blocks, directories as data, the interface the kernel exposes) is
[[OPERATING SYSTEMS]] material; see [[File Systems]].

The Python version is [[File I-O]] in [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTER SCIENCE]]: same open, process,
close, with `with` doing the closing and mode `"w"` truncating on open.
